snapshot.what_it_does: Polycab India Limited is India's largest electrical industry company by revenue, manufacturing and selling wires & cables (W&C) and fast-moving electrical goods (FMEG) such as switches, switchgear, solar products, fans and lighting. It also runs an EPC business and an international/export business, executing a five-year strategic plan called Project Spring.

segments.name: Wires & Cables (W&C)
segments.note: Revenue grew 33% YoY to ₹252 billion; EBITDA margin 13.9%; market share ~30-31% in India's organised W&C market

segments.name: FMEG
segments.note: Revenue up 25% YoY to ₹20,693 million; includes switches, switchgear, solar (3.5x volume growth), fans; profitable after Q4FY25 breakeven

segments.name: EPC
segments.note: Revenue ₹16.7 billion, down 13.2% YoY; EBIT ₹1.7 billion at 9.9% margin; ~₹80 billion BharatNet Phase-III contracts secured

snapshot.geographies: Primarily India (domestic business), with exports of ₹15,695 million contributing 5.4% of consolidated revenue, growing 16.7% YoY; footprint expanded to 94 countries (from 48 in FY19), with strong performance in the Middle East and Latin America; targeting exports >10% of revenue by FY30.
key_facts: Consolidated revenue ₹288,838 million, up 29% YoY; PAT ₹27,084 million, up 32% YoY
EBITDA grew 35% YoY with margins at 13.9%
Net cash position of ₹41,940 million; FY26 capex ₹14.8 billion (highest ever); planned capex ₹60–80 billion over five years
Credit ratings upgraded to CRISIL AAA/Stable and IND AAA/Stable (short-term CRISIL A1+ and IND A1+ reaffirmed)
Recommended dividend of ₹47 (470%) per ₹10 equity share; Project Spring targets W&C EBITDA margins 11–13% and FMEG margins 8–10%

promised_vs_delivered.verdict: Management's checkable near-term promises were largely met: Q4 margins improved, price pass-through landed, capex stayed within guidance, and exports rebounded as committed. Deviations were mostly favorable (working capital and W&C margins beat the guided ranges); EPC margins stayed lumpy and long-dated Project Spring targets remain untested.

bull.point: FY26 revenue ₹288,838m (+29%), PAT ₹27,084m (+32%), EBITDA +35% at 13.9% margin; India’s largest electricals player with ~30-31% organised W&C share.
Momentum accelerated: Q2 FY27 revenue +52.8% YoY, PAT +42.6%, EBITDA margin 14.4%; Q1/Q2 W&C EBIT margins 13.3%/14.2% beat Project Spring’s 11-13%.
Net cash ₹41,940m, CRISIL/IND AAA upgrades, ₹47 dividend; exports ₹15,695m (+16.7%) across 94 countries, targeting >10% of revenue by FY30.

bear.point: Concentration is high: W&C is 87% of revenue; EPC fell 13.2% YoY and margins were lumpy at 11% Q1 FY27, 7.2% Q2.
Margin risk: W&C EBIT ran above the 11-13% Project Spring band, while Q4 FY26 PAT grew only 6.3% despite revenue +26.9%.
Execution load: FY26 capex ₹14.8bn was highest ever within ₹60-80bn five-year plan; exports are 5.4% versus >10% FY30 goal.

watch: Q3 FY27 W&C EBIT margin versus 11-13% Project Spring range and whether commodity price pass-through holds.
Exports after Q2 FY27’s ~85% QoQ jump: order-book conversion toward >10% of revenue by FY30.
EPC margin stability/BharatNet execution and working-capital normalization from 11-15 days toward guided 50-55; no post-Q2 FY27 filings provided.
